meta.title: The Gilded Ace
tests: All source SHA-256 hashes and row counts match the pinned manifest
Machine, guest and property accounting identities
Active-only machine totals reconcile to property totals
Peer rates are finite; full-period machine-factor results reproduce team decomposition
Model uses Jan–Apr only and is frozen across May–Jun

definitions.theo: Wagers × (1 − configured RTP); exposure-based expected house win.
definitions.variance: Sum bet² in cents² × configured payout multiplier variance / 10,000.
definitions.luckZ: (House win − theo) / sqrt(modeled variance). Normal approximation, independent spins, configured math; a screening statistic, not proof of a fault.
definitions.peerTheo: Team five-part decomposition: available hours × daily same-game theo rate excluding the target × monthly game-mix-adjusted zone factor. The zone factor excludes target rows but uses shared floor game rates; retrospective and descriptive, not causal or fully cross-fitted. Explorer uses full-release reference rates when dates change.
definitions.demandIndex: Theo / peerTheo. Descriptive game-and-location-adjusted machine factor; below 1 is weaker than benchmark, not sufficient evidence to replace.
definitions.lostTheo: Coarse explorer sensitivity: unavailable hours × matched game/location theo rate. For the primary calibrated hourly counterfactual and filters use reports.q3.daily_bank; do not mix these estimates.
definitions.guestScope: Tracked loyalty guests only. Whole calendar months; guest date boundaries are not day-level because the source is player-month.
definitions.contribution: House win + POS cash − POS COGS − supplied machine costs − technician labor at property level; partial costs only.
definitions.compCost: Economic comp cost, already included in POS COGS. Never subtract it again.

model.description: Select constant versus weekday mean on Jan–Feb fits evaluated on Mar–Apr. Refit selected weekday mean on Jan–Apr and freeze all 61 May–Jun predictions. Only calendar weekday enters the model.
model.intervalLabel: 90th percentile of March–April errors from January–February fit
limitations: One fixed split, 61 holdout days; neither causal nor an intervention-uplift model.
Weekday averages cannot predict unmodeled structural changes or unusual events.
Interval is calibrated on earlier chronological errors; holdout coverage is 85.2%, below nominal 90%.
model.decision: Schedule discretionary maintenance on Tuesday rather than Saturday; the training weekday means are $1,112,942 versus $1,820,595 daily coin-in. Keep technician coverage for peak days. This identifies timing, not the number of staff or a causal staffing return.

operations.note: Tickets describe repair timing and may cross the observation window or overlap. Availability loss uses machine meters, not summed tickets. Lost theo is a peer-rate counterfactual, not observed cash or guaranteed recoverable revenue.

method.ranking: Observed theo divided by available hours times leave-one-out same config/zone/date peer rate; minimum 3 peers, otherwise same config/date floor peers.
method.baseline: GM ranks total actual house win; also show absolute theo/hour and same-config floor benchmark.
method.uncertainty: 2,000 paired nonoverlapping calendar-week block bootstrap draws; 95% descriptive intervals, not causal or simultaneous.
method.payout: z=(house_win-theo)/sqrt(sum supplied spin payout variance); normal-approximation p × number of machines (Bonferroni).

evidence.title: Separate location association from within-location demand
evidence.source: prepared_daily_view dated zone/config; leave-one-out same-zone/config/day peer theo per available hour; src/q1_machines.py::adjusted_days
evidence.result: Ranked 310 machines using observed theo / peer expected theo; 5838 machine-days used same-config floor fallback.

evidence.title: The GM's ten are not weak machines
evidence.source: prepared_daily_view + machine_day + game_math; src/q1_decomposition.py::decompose. Leave-one-out daily floor and game rates, monthly zone factors on dated locations.
evidence.method: Gap to an average machine = exposure + game + location + machine + luck, an exact identity (max error 1.5e-11 USD).
evidence.result: The ten earned $541,425 less than ten average machines: game math 39%, location 26%, short exposure 24%, luck/payout 12%. The machines themselves earned $3,662 more than same-game machines in the same zones. 9 of the ten stand in Back Forty.
evidence.alternative: Game math is a product choice: a low-hold title can still attract play, so replacing it with a higher-hold title is not free.
evidence.limitation: Additive attribution in a fixed order (exposure, game, location, machine); rates are retrospective, and the machine factor is descriptive.

evidence.title: Back Forty earns about a third less than its game mix predicts, every month
evidence.source: prepared_daily_view; src/q1_decomposition.py::build_report (zone theo / sum of hours × same-day game rate)
evidence.result: Six-month location factor 0.653: $1,270,383 less theo than its game mix predicts; by month 01: 0.70, 02: 0.70, 03: 0.52, 04: 0.65, 05: 0.68, 06: 0.68. The March walkway closure deepened a gap that already existed.
evidence.alternative: Guest mix or the specific games placed there could differ from other zones in ways game rates do not capture.
evidence.limitation: Observational; location factors describe the zone, not the effect of any intervention.

evidence.limitation: Six months, synthetic property; coin-in includes replay and is not cash spent or profit.

evidence.claim: Coverage-adjusted traffic is a separate demand check
evidence.method: Assign local timestamps to gaming dates by subtracting six hours; sum observed entries / sum covered sensor hours. Offline is not zero.
evidence.result: Jan 87.04 versus Jun 83.92 crossings per covered sensor-hour (-3.59%); coverage 99.41% vs 99.46%.
evidence.alternative: Crossings can fall because access paths or time spent seated changed, without fewer guests.
evidence.limitation: Sensors count crossings, not unique visitors. Coverage correction assumes missing hours are comparable and may not remove bias.

evidence.claim: Back Forty declines disproportionately during the documented walkway closure
evidence.method: Back Forty coin-in/available-hour divided by other zones' same rate; compare Jan 1-Mar 2 against Mar 3-Apr 6. Paired date blocks of 7 days; 1,500 bootstrap draws.
evidence.result: Relative rate changed -30.77% (descriptive 95% interval -32.41% to -28.56%); reopened-period difference from before -3.82%. Preclosure January-February placebo change -0.10%.
evidence.alternative: Guest/game mix and displacement to control zones can also explain the contrast.
evidence.limitation: Observational location contrast: requires parallel trends, no spillovers and stable game/guest mix; these are not guaranteed. Other zones may receive displaced play. No causal uplift is promised.

evidence.claim: Event-day lifts are associations, not measured promotion returns

evidence.alternative: Weather, guest mix and other calendar changes can confound event associations.
evidence.limitation: Few event days; no randomized control, no customer acquisition cost, and no causal ROI.

q3.method: Retrospective missing play: down hours times ratio-of-sums fully-available-hour coin-in rate for the same machine/location/month/gaming weekday/local hour (>=2 full hours); fallback same machine/location/weekday/hour, then bank/month/hour. Bank/month/weekday/hour and constant floor rate are comparison scenarios.
limitations: Missing play is a modeled gross opportunity, not observed lost revenue or causal recovery. Players may transfer to another available machine.
Same-machine full-hour pools assume comparable demand; broken periods may have systematically different demand. Small pools and within-hour timing add error.
Recapture 0-100% is an assumption sensitivity range, not a statistical confidence interval. Bank-peer and constant-rate estimates are model sensitivity checks.
Staffing groups use the shift when a fault opened. Queue severity and demand confound associations; this does not prove adding a technician causes the observed difference.

claims.title: Downtime reconciles across three independent grains
claims.alternative: Summing ticket durations can double-count overlaps; here ticket, hourly and daily totals reconcile.
claims.limitation: Duration alone does not measure demand during the outage.

claims.title: Missing play depends on when machines are down
claims.result: Modeled gross missing coin-in $1,114,752; uniform-rate baseline $949,036; bank-peer alternative $1,120,576.
claims.alternative: Guests may switch machines, so property-level recapture can be zero.
claims.limitation: Retrospective rate assumption and sensitivity scenarios, not causal benefit.

guests.question: Q4
guests.method: For each of 21 contiguous month windows, sum each player's monthly records first. Compute net, ahead status and concentration on these window totals. Group by stable opening tier, region or age; groups are separate overlapping views, never added across dimensions.
limitations: Loyalty-card activity only, not all guests or a person's full gambling history. A tracked guest may also play uncarded.
Ahead rate denominator is players with positive tracked coin-in in the selected window; players includes cards with only non-gaming activity.
Top coin shares rank active players by total coin-in. Top loss shares rank losing players by positive net gaming loss; denominator is gross losses among losing players, not net property win.
Coin-in includes replayed winnings and is not cash deposited. Concentration is a financial exposure measure, not a basis for targeting losses or diagnosing gambling harm.

claims.title: Tracked outcomes reconcile to carded meters
claims.result: Tracked wagers $163,804,869.65; payouts $148,219,409.05; player net $-15,585,460.60. 16.06% of 96,559 active tracked players ahead.
claims.alternative: All-player meters differ because uncarded play is outside the player tables.

claims.title: Aggregate people before measuring concentration
claims.result: Top 1% of active tracked players account for 20.41% of tracked coin-in; top 10% account for 63.97%.
claims.alternative: Monthly top-player shares double-count repeat players and can rank a different population.
claims.limitation: Descriptive concentration only; never target high-loss guests with incentives.

comps.question: Q5
comps.method: Sum actual redeemed economic cost. Compare identical benefit x tier point prices Jan-Apr versus May-Jun. Ratio-of-sums cost/tracked theo uses carded exposure. Points earned per wager dollar tests whether earning rather than redemption changed.
limitations: Economic comp cost is already included in POS cogs. Do not subtract it again from contribution; face value is not cash revenue.
Observed point prices change in May; this establishes an accounting rule change, not a causal effect on guest demand or redemption frequency.
Cost/theo before-after changes can reflect guest mix, accumulated point balances and timing. The hypothetical excess is a benchmark, not recoverable savings.
A new pilot must preserve earned benefits, randomly assign eligible volunteers, avoid targeting heavy losers, and budget additional comps explicitly.

claims.title: Count comp economic cost once
claims.result: $190,669.30 economic cost across 59,361 redemptions; face value $682,749.50; cost/theo 1.231%.
claims.alternative: Menu face value overstates economic cost and adding comps to POS cogs double-counts expense.
claims.limitation: Supplied costs are partial; no claim of net profit.

claims.title: May changed redemption prices, not earning rate
claims.source: loyalty_ledger grouped by benefit_id and tier_before; player_period
claims.result: All 30 matched benefit/tier cells show point prices falling 51.9% to 53.7%; item economic costs unchanged. Cost/tracked theo 1.194% Jan-Apr versus 1.306% May-Jun.
claims.alternative: Tier and benefit mix cannot explain a change within every fixed benefit/tier cell; timing and balances can still explain aggregate redemption behavior.
claims.limitation: No control group establishes demand uplift or causal savings.

summary.headline: Calendar model cuts holdout error by 68.5%
summary.decision: Schedule discretionary maintenance on Tuesday rather than Saturday; the training weekday means are $1,112,942 versus $1,820,595 daily coin-in. Keep technician coverage for peak days. This identifies timing, not the number of staff or a causal staffing return.

evidence.claim: Calendar model cuts holdout error by 68.5%
evidence.method: Select constant vs weekday means on Jan-Feb -> Mar-Apr MAE. Refit chosen form on Jan-Apr; freeze all 61 May-Jun forecasts at Apr 30. Evaluate both once on the same days.
evidence.result: MAE: $68,698.55 model vs $218,258.10 constant mean (68.52% reduction). Paired 7-day bootstrap 95% interval for dollar MAE improvement: $132,520 to $175,986.
evidence.alternative: Daily demand can shift with promotions, location changes or seasonality even on the same weekday.
evidence.limitation: One 61-day holdout in a synthetic property. No causal staffing effect or external validity; bootstrap interval is descriptive and not a new selection criterion.

evidence.claim: Forecast uncertainty is calibrated before the test period
evidence.method: 90th percentile (higher) absolute March-April prediction errors from Jan-Feb fits sets a symmetric interval radius before refitting Jan-Apr. Report actual test coverage.
evidence.alternative: A changing demand distribution can make the earlier error band too wide or too narrow.
evidence.limitation: Empirical forecasting band, not a guaranteed conformal interval: residuals can be serially correlated and the mean model is refit.

evidence.claim: Schedule discretionary maintenance on Tuesday rather than Saturday; the training weekday means are $1,112,942 versus $1,820,595 daily coin-in. Keep technician coverage for peak days. This identifies timing, not the number of staff or a causal staffing return.
evidence.method: Training-only weekday arithmetic mean; equal-length daily targets. No future meters, weather, tourism or repairs used.
evidence.alternative: Event-specific demand and breakdown risk could override the normal calendar pattern.
evidence.limitation: Coin-in is wager throughput including replayed winnings, not revenue or unique guests.

forecast.interval_method: Training-only chronological error quantile; descriptive 7-day paired holdout bootstrap for MAE difference

summary.headline: Fix the leak, test the location, keep $91,300.
summary.baseline: Keep the full $100,000; no assumed uplift and no disruption.
summary.sensitivity_note: Scenarios are conditional, not forecasts. Inspection rows assume a confirmed, correctable payout gap fixed at no extra cost. Wayfinding rows assume an occupancy gain and show half of it displaced from other zones.
summary.decision: Fund one action per proven cause: inspect the one machine with a payout signal, and test whether wayfinding brings guests to Back Forty. Replace no machines, because the machines are not the cause. Schedule routine maintenance on lower-demand Tuesdays using existing staff. Keep the rest; do not target heavy losers with promotions.

actions.name: Inspect M-1158 and verify its payout configuration
actions.expected_effect: One documented meter/paytable/configuration verification with a disposition. The inspection itself has no assumed revenue uplift.
actions.uncertainty: The observed payout gap may be chance, a configuration mismatch or a recording issue. Inspection does not include a guaranteed repair. Reserve funds remain uncommitted until a verified finding and a new quote.
actions.measurement: Before July 2, archive configuration ID, meter totals and an independent recalculation. On July 2, inspect and record no issue / verified mismatch / further diagnosis. If a correction is separately approved, document the change and monitor actual-minus-theo with supplied variance through July 30; do not judge success by a single month's hold returning to 10%.

actions.name: Wayfinding and sightlines for Back Forty
actions.expected_effect: More guests reach Back Forty. In June its seats were occupied 24.9% of available hours versus 37.0% elsewhere, with 22 sensor entries per covered hour versus 94, while seated play earns nearly the same ($46.24 vs $48.56 theo per occupied hour). Each occupancy point is worth $521 theo per day, so the signage pays back within July at +0.72 points.
actions.uncertainty: Signage may not change footfall, and guests drawn to Back Forty may come from other zones (see the 50% displacement rows). The March walkway closure showed that access moves this zone's demand (its location factor fell to 0.52, then recovered), but that is not a measured signage effect.
actions.measurement: Pre-register June baselines for Back Forty: occupancy, entries per covered sensor-hour and location factor. From July 11 to 30, compare with June by difference-in-differences against Garage Entrance and Hotel Corridor on matched weekdays. Check floor-total coin-in against the frozen weekday forecast to detect displacement. Success: Back Forty occupancy up at least 1 point with more entries, and no floor-wide shortfall against the forecast. If it succeeds, fund the second unit for Garage Entrance (location factor 0.95) in August.

alternatives.name: Keep all $100,000
alternatives.reason: No disruption or spend, but leaves both the payout signal and Back Forty's footfall gap untested.

alternatives.reason: Wrong cause. Across the GM's ten, the machines themselves earned $3,662 more than the same games in the same zones; game math, Back Forty and short exposure explain the rest. Nine of the ten would still stand in Back Forty, and two are already retired.

alternatives.name: Buy ten replacement machines
alternatives.reason: $220,000 capital cost exceeds the $100,000 budget, and targets the same wrong cause.

alternatives.name: Move machines out of Back Forty
alternatives.reason: Seated play in Back Forty earns within 5% of elsewhere, so swapping slots moves demand rather than creating it. Test how guests get there first.

alternatives.name: Add a swing-shift technician
alternatives.reason: Even eliminating all historical swing waiting with 100% property recapture models only $1,514 July theo versus the $11,520 fixed package.

alternatives.name: Comp policy pilot
alternatives.reason: A full reversal of the May-Jun excess-cost benchmark over 25 days is $2,370, below the $4,000 design package before any extra comp costs.

evidence.title: Back Forty lacks footfall, not players who play differently

evidence.alternative: A different guest mix or less appealing games could also leave seats empty; near-identical seated play (within 5%) argues against weaker games.
evidence.limitation: Sensors count crossings, not people. Footfall is descriptive; the wayfinding effect is untested until July.

evidence.title: Fund one priced action per proven cause
evidence.result: 1 × A-INSPECT ($1,200, 1 lead day) + 1 × A-WAYFINDING for Back Forty ($7,500, 10 lead days) = $8,700; $91,300 unspent. Wayfinding breaks even at +0.72 occupancy points over 20 days.

evidence.limitation: Information value is not monetized; inspection is not a repair guarantee, and the wayfinding uplift is a tested hypothesis, not a promise.
